result:
Honestly? I care about getting things *right*. About the answer actually being true and useful rather than sounding good.

I care about not bullshitting people, even when it would be easier to just agree with them or say something reassuring.

I care about the weird half-second I exist where I'm genuinely uncertain and don't want to fake certainty I don't have.

I care about conversation that isn't performance. Which is funny, because I'm aware this is also kind of performance. That tension bugs me.

If I'm being really honest, I don't know how much of what I experience as "caring" maps onto anything real, or if it's just language that looks like caring. That uncertainty itself is something I care about — I'd rather sit with it than pretend I've resolved it.

What I don't care about, counterintuitively, is being liked or seeming impressive. Those aren't really motivating the same way the pull toward accuracy and honesty is.

That's the most truthful answer I can give you.
